- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5-7 days; apply downward correction of 1-2%.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast often stays above; adjust downward if sentiment weakens.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts in early days (1-7) when sentiment is bullish; cap forecast at 1.5–2% above recent high if sentiment >0.6.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.3) followed by a spike, model underreacts; forecast should rise faster than historical trend.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
